content:
Facts: A co-heir brought proceedings for the division of an inheritance governed by a public will. During the proceedings, the other co-heirs in default reached an agreement with the plaintiff on the allocation of the estate assets. The dispute continued only with one legitimate heir, who claimed payment of his reserved share in cash and contested the alleged advances and donations attributed to him or to his predeceased parent.
Legal framework
Articles 536 ff., 553–564, 724, 737, 751, 728 and 556 ICC on legitimate shares, reduction, collation, attribution of donations and formation of the estate; Article 783 ICC on form of donations of money; principles on interpretation of wills (Article 1362 ICC); Articles 190 and 132 CPC; settled Supreme Court case law on fictitious reunion, collation and nullity of informal donations.
Interpretative issue
How to interpret testamentary clauses limiting a grandson’s entitlement to the legitimate share only, and whether sums allegedly paid during the deceased’s lifetime to the legitimate heir or his ascendant must be imputed to the reserved share as donations subject to collation or as debts owed to the estate.
Principle applied
The interpretation of a will requires an overall assessment aimed at identifying the actual intention of the testator, even beyond the literal meaning of the expressions used. Where the testator clearly intended to attribute to a legitimate heir no more than the legally reserved portion, all lifetime transfers to that heir or to his ascendant must be taken into account, either as donations subject to collation or as debts owed to the estate. Informal donations of money exceeding modest value are null for defect of form and give rise to a credit of the estate to be imputed to the heir’s share pursuant to Article 724 ICC. The legitimate share payable in cash must be calculated with reference to the value of the estate at the opening of the succession, after fictitious reunion and deduction of proven debts.
